A California traffic stop took a massive turn when a police K-9 sniffed out approximately 200 kilos, or roughly 440 pounds, of cocaine allegedly packed inside an SUV filled with cardboard boxes, authorities said.

The Alhambra Police Department said the incident began after officers conducted a traffic stop along Valley Boulevard near the 710 Freeway.

California voters will decide whether the state will charge a one-time tax on billionaires. The idea that has split Democrats and labor unions.

SCOTT SIMON, HOST:  A proposal on the ballot in California would charge that state's billionaires a one-time tax worth tens of billions of dollars in revenue. Senator Bernie Sanders is scheduled to be in California this weekend at rallies for the proposal. But other Democrats, including California's governor, Gavin Newsom, are campaigning against it. We're joined now by Marisa Lagos from KQED in San Francisco. Marisa, thanks so much for being with us.MARISA LAGOS, BYLINE: Thanks for having me.SIMON: What are voters being asked?LAGOS: Yeah. This is known as Proposition 40. It was proposed by a labor union that represents healthcare workers.
